P3j: So the question isn’t whether a person is “good enough” for community. Rather, whether the fit is right. Consider how much attention they currently have available for other people, how willing they are to examine their own reactions. And on the other hand, look at whether the group has enough free resource/capacity to support them without becoming a full-time caretaker operation.
P16j: I still don’t know how to keep this language of capacity from becoming a respectable way to exclude people who are disabled, poor, less articulate, maybe simply uncomfortable or unfamiliar with therapeutic language, or for whatever reason deemed inconvenient. Pretending capacity is unlimited won’t solve that. Any real process would need concrete criteria, review by someone who wasn’t part of the decision, and a way to revisit a “not now” decision on membership. Even then, the power to veto membership applications based on capacity remains dangerous.
